drivers.why_material: Company stated both Phase 3 trials had a 'projected enrollment goal of 1,360 patients' in March 2021 marketing, but CT.gov shows the actual trial (NCT03595553) was initially registered at 680 patients and later reduced to 355 actual enrollment. No version ever showed 1,360. This is a 2x fabrication of sample size for the catalyst trial itself, suggesting intentional masking of underpowered enrollment.

Company guided Q1 2022 topline in November 2021 press release, but CT.gov version 10 (filed September 2021, two months prior) already showed primary completion had slipped to September 2021—three months past original target. The company continued to guide forward despite the trial already being overdue, a pattern consistent with delaying bad news.

dismissed.why_not_material: This is standard early-stage promotion citing Phase 2 microbiome data as supportive color for the mechanism. The Phase 3 catalyst trials are properly randomized head-to-head comparisons, so referencing earlier open-label microbiome findings alongside the pivotal program is normal IR, not masking of the catalyst trial itself (principle #3).

Same rationale as smmt_004: citing prior Phase 2 microbiome data in marketing while running a randomized Phase 3 is standard promotional context, not manipulation of the catalyst trial's basis or design.

analyst_note: EXCLUDE from long basket. Summit fabricated the Phase 3 enrollment figures for the catalyst trials, claiming 1,360 patients when CT.gov never showed anything close—the actual trial enrolled 355. This is not a restatement or rounding error; it's a 2x overstatement of sample size for the exact catalyst readout. Additionally, the company guided Q1 2022 topline in November 2021 despite CT.gov already showing (in the September filing) that primary completion had slipped to September 2021, three months overdue. Together, these constitute direct masking of underpowered enrollment and timeline slippage on the catalyst trial itself. The two minor findings on Phase 2 microbiome claims are dismissed as normal early-stage promotion and do not bear on the Phase 3 catalyst honesty.
